items.title: Return foreign-address certification form
items.quote: Please complete the enclosed address certification and mail or upload it by January 15, 2027.
items.computation: The letter gives an explicit calendar date as the deadline ('by January 15, 2027'), not a period to be counted. This is a US bank, not a German authority or court, so the German delivery-fiction rules (§122 AO, §41 VwVfG, §37 SGB X) and the weekend/holiday-shift rules for legal periods do not apply; the stated date is used as written. January 15, 2027 falls on a Friday, so no adjustment would be needed in any case.

warnings: The sender is a US bank (Iowa) writing to a customer in Germany; verify this is genuinely from your bank (e.g. via the number on your card or bank statement) before mailing or uploading any personal address-certification form, since unsolicited requests for personal documents by mail/email are a common phishing pattern.

The letter threatens restricted online access if the form is not received, which is a common pressure tactic used in scam letters, even though this could also be a legitimate federal (US) compliance requirement for customers residing abroad.
